api:
<Choropleth data={values} regions={shapes} name={|v: &Value| v.region.as_ref()} value={|v: &Value| v.amount} />
PropTypeDefault
dataone row per region with a valuerequired
regionsVec<Region> or Signal<Vec<Region>>: the shapesrequired
nameFn(&T) -> &str: matched against Region::namerequired
valueFn(&T) -> f64required
projectionProjection::Equirectangular, Mercator or Plane (x, y as given)Equirectangular
schemeHeatmapSchemeBlues
range(f64, f64)the data's minimum and maximum
decimalsusizeas needed
scale_barbooltrue

Region::new(name, rings) takes polygon rings of (longitude, latitude) (or (x, y) with Plane). Every ring is filled, so islands work; holes are not cut out. Regions without a value are grey. Keep regions in a signal: the map is recomputed only when it or the data changes.

examples.title: US tile map
examples.description: One square per state coloured by value; hover a state.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn states() {
    let (regions, data) = (use_signal(tiles()), use_signal(state_values(1, 100.)));
    rsx! { <Choropleth data={data} regions={regions} name={|s: &Stat| s.region.as_ref()} value={|s: &Stat| s.value} projection={Projection::Plane} class="h-80" /> }
}

examples.title: Missing data
examples.description: Regions without a value are grey.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn missing() {
    let regions = use_signal(tiles());
    let data = use_signal(
        state_values(2, 100.)
            .into_iter()
            .step_by(2)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    rsx! { <Choropleth data={data} regions={regions} name={|s: &Stat| s.region.as_ref()} value={|s: &Stat| s.value} projection={Projection::Plane} scheme={HeatmapScheme::Purples} class="h-80" /> }
}

examples.title: Diverging scale
examples.description: A fixed −10 to 10 range on a red–blue scheme.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn diverging() {
    let regions = use_signal(tiles());
    let data = use_signal(
        state_values(3, 20.)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|stat| Stat {
                value: stat.value - 10.,
                ..stat
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    rsx! { <Choropleth data={data} regions={regions} name={|s: &Stat| s.region.as_ref()} value={|s: &Stat| s.value} projection={Projection::Plane} scheme={HeatmapScheme::RdBu} range={(-10., 10.)} class="h-80" /> }
}

examples.title: Hexagon districts
examples.description: Any polygons work; these are hexagons.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn hex_districts() {
    let (regions, data) = (use_signal(hexes(8, 6)), use_signal(districts(4)));
    rsx! { <Choropleth data={data} regions={regions} name={|s: &Stat| s.region.as_ref()} value={|s: &Stat| s.value} projection={Projection::Plane} scheme={HeatmapScheme::Viridis} decimals={1} class="h-80" /> }
}

examples.title: Continents
examples.description: Longitude and latitude, plotted as they are.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn world_equirectangular() {
    let regions = use_signal(continents());
    let data = use_signal(named(&[
        ("North America", 600.),
        ("South America", 430.),
        ("Europe", 745.),
        ("Africa", 1400.),
        ("Asia", 4700.),
        ("Oceania", 45.),
    ]));
    rsx! { <Choropleth data={data} regions={regions} name={|s: &Stat| s.region.as_ref()} value={|s: &Stat| s.value} scheme={HeatmapScheme::Oranges} class="h-80" /> }
}

examples.title: Fixed range
examples.description: range 0–100 keeps colours comparable between maps.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn fixed_range() {
    let (regions, data) = (use_signal(hexes(10, 5)), use_signal(districts(7)));
    rsx! { <Choropleth data={data} regions={regions} name={|s: &Stat| s.region.as_ref()} value={|s: &Stat| s.value} projection={Projection::Plane} range={(0., 100.)} scheme={HeatmapScheme::Magma} class="h-80" /> }
}

examples.title: Turnout
examples.code:
#[component]
fn turnout() {
    let (regions, data) = (
        use_signal(island()),
        use_signal(
            provinces(8)
                .into_iter()
                .map(|stat| Stat {
                    value: 40. + stat.value % 50.,
                    ..stat
                })
                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
        ),
    );
    rsx! { <Choropleth data={data} regions={regions} name={|s: &Stat| s.region.as_ref()} value={|s: &Stat| s.value} projection={Projection::Plane} scheme={HeatmapScheme::Cividis} decimals={0} class="h-80" /> }
}
